reviewer.actual_effort: I looked at all 9 enlarged PNGs listed in return-details/manifest.json first and formed a reading for each. Only then did I read shofar-completion-return-a/review.json and shofar-completion-return-b/review.json. Neither prior review changed my readings. I opened no other files. The crops are blurry, and I could only view them at the size shown, with no extra zoom.

readings.name: kenesiyyot

marks.yod_dagesh: present: a separate dot sits at mid-height just left of the small yod, between the yod and the vav. It is not the holam, which sits above the vav.

unresolved: Small yods in this typeface leave little room inside the letter, so the dagesh is printed beside the yod, not inside it. I read that dot as the yod's dagesh. Confidence is moderate to high.

readings.name: lo

marks.lamed_dagesh: not visible in this crop: I see no dot inside the lamed's lower bowl
marks.vav: holam male: a dot at the top left of the vav

unresolved: This disagrees with the primary reading (lamed dagesh YES). This crop is the most blurred of the nine, and a faint dot could be lost in the dark lamed stroke. I am not supplying the dagesh from the Masoretic Text. A crop at native resolution is needed to decide.

marks.final_kaf_dagesh: present: a clear dot inside the final kaf's upper bowl

readings.name: tehilla

marks.tav_dagesh: probably present: a dot sits low inside the tav, just above the sheva and inside the letter's outline

unresolved: The dot is low, near the tav/he boundary, and slightly toward the he. I can't fully rule out that it is the he's hiriq set high and to the right. I read it as the tav's dagesh, but not with confidence.

readings.name: dorshav

marks.yod_between_shin_and_vav: not seen: only one letter follows the shin, and it is full height down to the baseline, so it is a vav. There is no separate short yod stroke.

unresolved: My own reading agrees with review B's דֹּרְשָׁו, but I did not take it from that review. At this resolution, a yod touching the vav could merge into it. I recommend not deleting the yod until a native-resolution crop confirms it.

readings.name: huazeh

marks.maqaf_hua_zeh: none visible: the two words are set very close or touching, with no raised horizontal stroke between them. The comparable line 3 'הוּא מֶלֶךְ' also has no maqaf.

unresolved: The tight setting could hide a short maqaf where the alef meets the zayin. I lean toward 'no maqaf' but am not confident.

readings.name: ps24-opening

marks.divine_name: lamed patah, nothing on the yod, qamatz under the vav. I see no separate oleh or meteg stroke apart from the lamed's own ascender.
marks.haaretz: he qamatz, alef qamatz, resh segol. There is an extra short vertical stroke under the alef, beside its qamatz, which I read as a meteg on the alef.

unresolved: Haaretz: the stroke under the alef is visible, and alef is its likely host. At this size I can't tell a meteg from a similar vertical accent, or rule out the resh as host.
Divine name: I can't find any high stroke apart from the lamed ascender. Whether a separate oleh exists there is unresolved, and I am not supplying one.

marks.second_tav_vowel: segol: three dots, two above and one centred below, not tsere's two dots side by side

marks.chet_vowel: patah: a single horizontal bar with no stem below it

limits: These readings come only from the 9 manifest crops. I did not open the native scans s192, s194, s196 or s198. lo, tehilla, dorshav, huazeh and ps24-opening should be checked against native-resolution crops of those exact spots.

My readings disagree with the primary narrow readings at one site: lo has no visible lamed dagesh. They agree with the primary at kenesiyyot, avarkhekha, shetitten and sholkhai, and lean toward it at tehilla. At dorshav, huazeh and ps24-opening my readings are tentative, so I give a lean, not a confident call.
No mark was copied from another occurrence of the same word or from Masoretic Text expectations. I make no claims about acceptance, schema, compiler or export.
